questions.q: What question does function security answer in Oracle Fusion reporting?
options: Which specific rows of data a user can see
Whether a user can open a given reporting tool or piece of content at all
How fast a report runs
Which file format a report exports to
questions.explain: Function security, governed by duty roles, decides whether a user can even open a tool or a piece of catalog content.

questions.q: What question does data security answer in Oracle Fusion reporting?
options: Whether the catalog folder exists
Given that a user can open a tool, which rows of data they are actually allowed to see
Whether a report can be scheduled
Which reporting tool a company has purchased
questions.explain: Data security, enforced through mechanisms like data access sets, filters the rows returned once a user is inside a tool they have function access to.

questions.q: Two users run the exact same OTBI analysis and get different results. What is the most likely explanation?
options: The analysis is broken and needs to be rebuilt
OTBI randomizes results between users
Their data security (such as data access set scope) differs, legitimately filtering the rows each of them sees
Only one of the users is allowed to use OTBI at all
questions.explain: The same analysis can correctly return different result sets because each user's data security scopes the underlying data differently.

questions.q: A user has a duty role granting access to the Payables subject area in OTBI. Does this automatically grant access to the General Ledger subject area too?
options: Yes, all subject areas are granted together automatically
No — each product-area subject area is typically granted by its own duty role
Only if the user also has a BI Publisher role
Subject areas have no relationship to duty roles
questions.explain: Access to specific OTBI subject areas is granted through duty roles tied to the underlying product; Payables access does not automatically include General Ledger access.

questions.q: Why do OTBI, BI Publisher, Financial Reporting Studio, and Smart View all share the same underlying security model instead of each having its own rules?
options: It was simpler for Oracle's engineers to build that way with no other benefit
So that a user's reporting access can never be broader than their transactional access in the application
Because only one of the four tools actually has any security
Security only applies to BI Publisher; the other three tools are unrestricted
questions.explain: Sharing one security model is a deliberate design choice: it prevents a user from seeing more in reports than they could already see in the transactional work areas.
